title: The quest to keep organs alive outside the body

paragraphs.text: This week, I covered a fascinating effort to preserve organs outside the body. There’s a huge shortage of donor organs, and one of the main reasons is time—they survive only a matter of hours outside the body, even when they’re kept on ice.
paragraphs.translation: 本週，我報導了一項關於在體外保存器官的引人注目的努力。捐贈器官嚴重短缺，其中一個主要原因是時間——即使保存在冰上，它們在體外也只能存活幾個小時。

paragraphs.text: Doctors dream of organ banks—stores of human organs that can be preserved for days, weeks, months, or even longer. That would allow them to run tests on organs, find the best matches for them, and transport the organs to those recipients.
paragraphs.translation: 醫生們夢想著建立器官庫——儲存可以保存數天、數週、數月甚至更長時間的人類器官。這將使他們能夠對器官進行測試，為其找到最佳匹配，並將器官運送給那些受捐者。

paragraphs.text: In new research, one team has been able to supercool the kidneys of pigs—animals whose organs are of a similar size to human ones—and preserve them for days. The kidneys survived being stored at −4 °C (25 °F) and eventually reimplanted back into pigs. And that’s just the latest development in a field that is positively buzzing.
paragraphs.translation: 在新的研究中，一個團隊已經能夠「超低溫冷卻」豬的腎臟——豬的器官大小與人類相似——並將其保存數天。這些腎臟在 -4 °C (25 °F) 的環境下儲存後存活，並最終重新植入豬體內。這只是一個正蓬勃發展領域的最新進展。

paragraphs.text: It has proved super difficult to freeze organs. Once ice forms in them, they’re done. The ice crystals create all kinds of damage and render the organs unusable. That hasn’t stopped many researchers from trying.
paragraphs.translation: 事實證明，冷凍器官非常困難。一旦其中形成冰晶，器官就毀了。冰晶會造成各種損害並導致器官無法使用。這並沒有阻止許多研究人員嘗試。

paragraphs.text: Some have focused on cryopreservation—rapid extreme cooling that essentially leaves cells in a glasslike state. This process is now routine for eggs, sperm, and embryos, which are cooled to −196 °C in less than two seconds and can be used even after decades in storage.
paragraphs.translation: 一些人專注於低溫保存——快速極端冷卻，基本上讓細胞處於玻璃狀狀態。這個過程現在對卵子、精子和胚胎來說已經是常規程序，它們在不到兩秒鐘的時間內被冷卻到 -196 °C，即使儲存數十年後仍可使用。

paragraphs.text: No one has managed to cryopreserve and thaw human organs for transplantation. But plenty of human bodies and brains have been stored at ultra-low temperatures in the hope that they might one day be rewarmed and brought back to life. (You can read more about why some people opt for cryonics here.)
paragraphs.translation: 目前還沒有人成功地為移植而低溫保存並解凍人類器官。但已有許多人類遺體和腦部被儲存在極低溫度下，希望能有一天被重新加熱並復活。（你可以在這裡閱讀更多關於為什麼有些人選擇人體冷凍術的原因。）

paragraphs.text: In March, I wrote about Stephen L. Coles, a gerontologist who had opted to cryopreserve his own brain. After the scientist died in 2014, his body was taken to Alcor, a cryonics facility in Arizona. A team at the facility removed Coles’s head, perfused his brain with cryoprotective chemicals (which work like antifreeze), removed the brain from the skull, and cooled it to −146 °C.
paragraphs.translation: 三月時，我寫過關於史蒂芬·L·科爾斯的故事，他是一位選擇低溫保存自己大腦的老年學家。這位科學家在 2014 年去世後，他的遺體被送往亞利桑那州的 Alcor，這是一家冷凍保存機構。該機構的一個團隊移除了科爾斯的頭部，在他的腦部灌流了低溫保護化學劑（作用類似於抗凍劑），將大腦從頭骨中取出，並冷卻至 -146 °C。

paragraphs.text: When Coles’s friend Greg Fahy, a cryobiologist, studied pieces of his brain years later, he found that the brain cells, which had shrunk, “bounced back” once they were rewarmed. But that doesn’t mean the cells are alive, or that it might one day be possible to reanimate the brain. As Matthew Powell Palm of Texas A&M told me at the time: “There are so many ways those neurons could be toast.”
paragraphs.translation: 當科爾斯的朋友、低溫生物學家格雷格·法希在多年後研究他的腦部切片時，他發現原本萎縮的腦細胞在重新加熱後「恢復了活力」。但這並不意味著細胞是活的，或者有一天可能讓大腦復活。正如德州農工大學的馬修·包威爾·帕姆當時告訴我的：「神經元有太多種方式可能會徹底報銷。」

paragraphs.text: Powell Palm is working on other ways to preserve organs. It was he, along with his colleagues, who managed to store supercooled pig kidneys and successfully transplant them, in a study described as “a landmark achievement.” Those organs did better than kidneys stored on ice, he says.
paragraphs.translation: 包威爾·帕姆正在研究其他保存器官的方法。正是他和他的同事們在一項被描述為「里程碑式成就」的研究中，成功地儲存了超低溫豬腎並成功完成移植。他說，這些器官的表現比保存在冰上的腎臟更好。

paragraphs.text: His approach didn’t require cryoprotectants. But other teams are exploring potential chemical cocktails that might allow them to store organs at lower temperatures, potentially for longer periods of time. (More on this in The Checkup soon!)
paragraphs.translation: 他的方法不需要低溫保護劑。但其他團隊正在探索潛在的化學雞尾酒配方，這可能使他們能夠在更低的溫度下保存器官，且時間可能更長。（更多關於此內容請見即將推出的《The Checkup》！）

paragraphs.text: Another way to prolong the lifespan of an organ is to use a machine that perfuses it with nutrients, mimicking what happens inside the body. Machine perfusion devices have become more commonly used over the last decade or so and are typically used to maintain livers and kidneys for up to about 24 hours.
paragraphs.translation: 延長器官壽命的另一種方法是使用機器為其灌流營養物質，模仿體內發生的情況。機器灌流裝置在過去十年左右的時間裡變得更加常用，通常用於維持肝臟和腎臟長達約 24 小時。

paragraphs.text: Researchers are now adapting this protocol for a growing list of organs, even eyeballs—a recent feat that might enable whole-eye transplants. In March, I went to visit scientists in Valencia who had developed a perfusion system for uteruses. They had used their device—which they nicknamed “Mother”—to keep a human uterus alive for a day.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人員現在正將此方案應用於越來越多的器官，甚至包括眼球——最近的一項壯舉可能使全眼移植成為可能。三月時，我前往瓦倫西亞拜訪了開發子宮灌流系統的科學家。他們使用被暱稱為「母親」的裝置，讓一個人類子宮存活了一天。

paragraphs.text: It’s an exciting time for organ preservation. Keep an eye out for more coverage from MIT Technology Review in the coming weeks.
paragraphs.translation: 對於器官保存來說，這是一個令人興奮的時刻。請在未來幾週繼續關注《麻省理工科技評論》的更多報導。

paragraphs.text: This article first appeared in The Checkup, MIT Technology Review’s weekly biotech newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Thursday, and read articles like this first, sign up here.
paragraphs.translation: 這篇文章最初出現在《The Checkup》，這是《麻省理工科技評論》每週一次的生物技術電子報。要在每週四收到它，並第一時間閱讀此類文章，請在此註冊。

paragraphs.text: Biotechnology and health
paragraphs.translation: 生物技術與健康

paragraphs.text: China has approved the world’s first invasive brain-computer chip—here’s what’s next
paragraphs.translation: 中國已批准全球首款侵入式腦機芯片——接下來會發生什麼

paragraphs.text: The country wants to become a global leader in brain implants. Strong government support is expected to help accelerate that process.
paragraphs.translation: 該國希望成為大腦植入物的全球領導者。強大的政府支持預計將有助於加速這一進程。

paragraphs.text: The “steroid olympics” were a circus—and a window into our culture
paragraphs.translation: 「類固醇奧運會」是一場鬧劇——也是窺視我們文化的一扇窗

paragraphs.text: Dozens of athletes on performance-enhancing drugs competed in the Enhanced Games. Organizers hope it'll sell a lot of peptides and other supplements.
paragraphs.translation: 數十名使用性能增強藥物的運動員參加了「增強運動會」。主辦方希望這能帶動大量胜肽和其他補充劑的銷售。

paragraphs.text: Sperm donors need limits, says a European fertility group
paragraphs.translation: 歐洲生育組織表示，精子捐贈者需要設限

paragraphs.text: Some donor-conceived people are finding hundreds of siblings. An international cap on donations could help prevent that.
paragraphs.translation: 一些由捐贈受孕的人發現自己有數百個兄弟姐妹。對捐贈次數設定國際上限可能有助於防止這種情況發生。

paragraphs.text: Inside interoception: The hidden sense of how you feel inside
paragraphs.translation: 內省覺察：關於你內在感受的隱藏感覺

paragraphs.text: Researchers are decoding how signals move between body and brain, with implications for how we understand and treat conditions from obesity to anxiety.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人員正在解碼信號如何在身體和大腦之間移動，這對於我們理解和治療從肥胖到焦慮等疾病具有啟發意義。

paragraphs.translation: 獲取《麻省理工科技評論》的最新更新

paragraphs.translation: 發現特別優惠、熱門故事、即將舉行的活動等。

quiz.sentence_zh: 長期停電會使安全系統完全失效。

quiz.sentence_zh: 每天早上檢查電子郵件已成為我日常慣例的一部分。

quiz.sentence: Modern technology aims to ____ the development of sustainable energy sources.
quiz.sentence_zh: 現代技術旨在加速永續能源的發展。

quiz.sentence_zh: 這間新的健身機構提供各種課程，包括瑜伽和重量訓練。

quiz.sentence: After the economic crisis, the city's tourism industry began to ____ slowly.
quiz.sentence_zh: 經濟危機過後，該市的旅遊業開始緩慢恢復活力。

quiz.sentence: You should ____ the latest job openings on the company's official website.
quiz.sentence_zh: 你應該留意公司官網上最新的職位空缺。
